question.leadin: During one of this general's campaigns, railroad ties were melted and twisted into loops to render them unusable.
question.text: Name this US general who led a scorched-earth "March to the Sea" through Georgia during the Civil War.
question.clue: This military leader issued "Special Field Orders Number 15," demanding parcels of 40 acres be given to freed slaves.

swap.text: The first of the Reconstruction Amendments is this one, which replaced the Emancipation Proclamation and banned slavery in the United States.
swap.clue: Its text was based on a portion of the Northwest Ordinance, and much of its jurisprudence concerns "badges and incidents."

question.text: This Mississippi city was captured by Union forces after a month long siege. Its capture ended Confederate control of the Mississippi River.
question.clue: It's not Atlanta, but the first bottling of Coca-Cola took place here in 1891.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about famous speeches in American history.
swap.text: This short speech by Abraham Lincoln given on a Pennsylvania battlefield challenged listeners to return to the ideals of a nation established "four score and seven years ago."
swap.clue: This speech declares the world "can never forget what they did here" to those interred at the Soldiers' National Cemetery.

question.leadin: He teamed up with Thaddeus Stevens as leaders of the Radical Republicans during Congressional Reconstruction.
question.text: Identify this Massachusetts Senator who argued against slavery in his "Crime Against Kansas" speech, and also attacked Stephen Douglas and Andrew Butler in anther speech denouncing the Kansas-Nebraska Act.
question.clue: This man had earlier described Stephen Douglass as the "Sancho Panza" to a man derided for his "incoherent phrases" and hoped that "South Carolina" would " howling."

swap.text: After repeated repulsions by the Union flank, Lee attempted a disastrous charge on the center of the Union front named for this Virginian Major General.
swap.clue: Another king of this name gave a 1939 speech from the throne despite his stammer.

question.text: After pro-slavery forces from Lecompton sacked the town of Lawrence, this abolitionist perpetrated the Pottawatomie Massacre in revenge. This abolitionist's most famous action was funded by the "Secret Six."
question.clue: This man was financed by Thomas Wentworth Higginson and other members of the "Secret Six."

swap.text: This Confederate general at Antietam was nicknamed "Old War Horse" by Robert Lee following the battle, and was later critically wounded at the Battle of the Wilderness.
swap.clue: He unsuccessfully besieged Knoxville and went on the defensive at Sharpsburg and Fredericksburg, where he held Marye's Heights.

question.text: This man, who was appointed Secretary of the Treasury after William Duane, finally pulled money out of the Bank as Jackson asked.
question.clue: After replacing William Duane, he ordered the end of federal deposits into the Second Bank of the United States as Secretary of the Treasury, but Jackson's bid to replace Gabriel Duvall with this man was a failure.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about peace negotiations for the Civil War.
swap.text: At Hampton Roads, the Confederacy was primarily represented by this Georgia native, who also served as its only vice president.
swap.clue: This Whig joined with his in-state rival, Democrat Howell Cobb, to create the first incarnation of the Constitutional Union Party, which helped elect his close ally Robert Toombs to the Senate.

question.text: This Confederate general fought at Fredericksburg and would later be killed by friendly fire at Chancellorsville. He earned his famous nickname by standing his ground at the First Battle of Bull Run.
question.clue: In another battle, this man's timely arrival with his namesake brigade managed to hold the line at Matthews Hill.

swap.text: Other early works about domesticity were written by Catharine from this family. Anti-slavery preachers like Lyman and Henry Ward were members of this family, which nicknamed firearms called "[this family's] Bibles."
swap.answerHtml: Beecher family [accept Catharine Beecher; accept Lyman Beecher; accept Henry Ward Beecher; accept Beecher’s Bibles]
swap.clue: Another member of this family used the New England Emigrant Aid Society to ship supplies for use against the Border Ruffians: Sharps Rifles known as his namesake "bibles."

question.text: Prentiss and Wallace fortified this position along a sunken road during the Battle of Shiloh. It held for about seven hours, allowing Grant to form a defensive position around Pittsburgh Landing.
question.clue: Popularly called the "sunken road", this nickname was given to the position of the main Union defensive line, made up of troops under Benjamin Prentiss and WHL Wallace. Prentiss and 2,200 others were captured here.

swap.leadin: William Seward introduced this amendment into the Senate, which would have prevented the federal government from interfering in "domestic institutions" of the states.
swap.text: Name this amendment that attempted to provide a compromise and stave off the Civil War. It passed the Senate but only five states ratified it before the Civil War.
swap.clue: This amendment, an attempt to deal with the slavery question, would have amended the Constitution to prevent further amendments pertaining to slavery.

question.leadin: The victims during this incident were on their way to Fort Lyon to make peace with Major Wynkoop, and the perpetrators ignored the white and American flags the victims were flying.
question.text: Name this incident in which troops under Colonel John Chivington opened fire on an encampment of Cheyenne and Arapaho Native Americans in Colorado.
question.clue: In 2014, Governor John Hickenlooper formally apologized for this event, which took place in modern-day Kiowa County and was carried out by the soldiers of John Chivington, despite the flag of peace flown by Black Kettle.

swap.text: During the Civil War, this woman earned the nickname "Angel of the Battlefield" for her work in bringing supplies to wounded soldiers at Antietam and elsewhere. This woman founded the American Red Cross in 1881.
swap.clue: On account of her friendship with Louis Appia, she lobbied the U.S. to attend the first Geneva Convention, and she read the book A Memory of Solferino.

question.leadin: This politician was dubbed "the Lion of White Hall" in reference to his family home in Kentucky, where he founded the abolitionist newspaper True American in Lexington in 1845.
question.text: Name this Kentucky planter who was named Minister to Russia by Abraham Lincoln at the very start of the Civil War, in which role he drummed up Russian support for the Union.
question.clue: He resigned his generalship in the Union Army when Lincoln would not immediately emancipate all slaves.

swap.leadin: In the aftermath of this event, a mob destroyed the office of the German-language Wecker, and Thomas Holliday Hicks authorized state militia to burn railway bridges into the affected city.
swap.text: Name this event in 1861 in which the Sixth Massachusetts Militia was assaulted by a mob while transitioning between rail stations on its journey south.

question.leadin: This man took many of his most iconic photos on Clarence King's 40th Parallel Survey, and allegedly developed photos inside of his mule-drawn "what is it wagon". FTPE.
question.text: Identify this American Civil War photographer who took the picture "The Harvest of Death" at Gettysburg and one of the first interior shots of a mine, "Cave-in, Gould & Curry Mine, Virginia City, Nevada".

swap.text: This doctor became the first globally known medical professional from the U.S. for discovering how to repair vesicovaginal fistula, a method he discovered through extensive gruesome experimentation on slave women.
swap.clue: This American "father of gynecology" who modified shoemaker's tools into a namesake catheter during terrible experiments on his own slaves.
